questions.q: Is "Activity" a real, standalone Salesforce object?
options: No — it's an umbrella term/shared UI grouping covering two real objects, Task and Event
Yes, it's a single standard object with its own fields
Yes, but only in Service Cloud
No, because Salesforce doesn't track calls or meetings at all
questions.explain: Activities refers to Task and Event together, grouped in a shared related list, but they are two distinct underlying objects.

options: An action item without a fixed calendar time, like a follow-up call or sending a proposal
A meeting scheduled at a specific start and end time
A closed Opportunity
A customer support Case
questions.explain: Task is for action items with a Status and often a Due Date, but no specific calendar time.

options: Something scheduled at a specific time, like a meeting with a defined start and end time
An action item with no fixed time
A Lead that has not yet been qualified
A Campaign Member's status
questions.explain: Event is the calendar-time object — a meeting or call with a defined start and end.

questions.q: Which standard objects can Tasks and Events be related to, per this lesson?
options: A Lead, a Contact, an Opportunity, or a Case
Only the Campaign object
Only the Account object
They cannot be related to any other object
questions.explain: Task and Event can relate to Leads, Contacts, Opportunities, or Cases, which is what enables a full activity history on those records.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say Activity history matters for analysis, beyond just Opportunity Stage and Amount?
options: Because two Opportunities with identical Amount and Stage can have very different Activity histories, and that difference often predicts whether a deal closes
Because Activities always match exactly with Opportunity Stage, so they're redundant
Because Task and Event records are never related to Opportunities
Because Activities replace the need for the Stage field entirely
questions.explain: Activity history is often the most direct evidence of real sales effort, which Stage and Amount alone don't capture.
